transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~43m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO, Sycamore), Lina Ortiz (Lead ML Eng), Omar Haddad (Platform)
Links shared: Redwood intro deck (link), integration guide (link), security pack (link /docs/security-pack.pdf)

Summary: quick discovery focused on integration options for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary use-cases: document QA + semantic search plus a few low-latency chat endpoints. Customer wants LangChain/LlamaIndex integration examples, gateway/proxy setup guidance, and clarity around rate limits/quotas and observability hooks for their SREs.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, I see folks on the line, quick intros — alex from redwood, priya is our solutions eng, and we can go around?
00:08 Daniel Park: hi i'm daniel, cto at sycamore ops, we run internal ops tooling and a customer-facing knowledge base, we're evaluating options to power semantic search and ai-assist in product
00:18 Lina Ortiz: lina here, lead ml eng, i'll own the POC and eval the integration.
00:25 Omar Haddad: omar, platform eng, i'll look after infra and security questions.
00:30 Priya Singh: great thanks, quick agenda: integration patterns (sdk, langchain/llamaindex), gateway/proxy and firewall concerns, rate limiting and quotas, observability/tracing hooks, and next steps.

02:04 Alex Chen: to set context what are your core constraints — latency targets and whether data residency or on-premision matters?
02:12 Daniel Park: two main constraints: sub-200ms p95 for our inline assistant calls (low context, prompt ~50 tokens) and cost sensitivity for batch semantic search. Also we have strict data retention rules for customer PII — so private deployment may be required for some flows but we want to understand tradeoffs.
02:35 Priya Singh: ok makes sense. For sub-200ms inline you typically want dedicated capacity close to your region or private on-prem with pinned GPUs. Hosted can be very fast but depends on model size and chosen instance; we can run dedicated latency benchmarks.

05:10 Lina Ortiz: can you walk through SDK story — we use python microservices and a nodejs front-end and many of our data connectors are built around LangChain and LlamaIndex.
05:22 Priya Singh: sure — we have first-class SDKs in python and node, and we maintain example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. For py you can do a direct Redwood client call or use the LangChain Redwood wrapper; same for LlamaIndex, we have a sample repo that shows document loader -> index -> retriever with Redwood embeddings and then a generation step. I'll share that repo link after the call.
05:45 Daniel Park: is the LangChain integration maintained upstream or copy in your examples? we've seen forks that bitrot.
05:51 Priya Singh: good Q — our examples are kept current and we contribute patterns back to the community. We also publish a dedicated Redwood LangChain cookbook with tested prompt templates.

08:10 Omar Haddad: network side, our infra sits in a private VPC and everything goes through a gateway/proxy. How does Redwood work with a customer proxy? can we route through a NAT or a forward proxy?
08:23 Priya Singh: for Hosted we allow requests from customer-owned static egress IP ranges for allowlisting and support HTTP proxies. For Dedicated/Private you can deploy a customer-facing gateway in your VPC which talks to Redwood control plane; for fully on-prem the runtime sits in your network so no egress needed. There can be a bit of work for mutual TLS if you want mTLS between gateway and runtime but we have patterns.

11:02 Daniel Park: ok and what about rate limits and quotas — we have bursty traffic during shift changes and need predictable throttling and backpressure.
11:12 Alex Chen: Hosted has tenant-level rate limits (configurable with tiers) and soft-burst windows; Dedicated gives you guaranteed throughput plus configurable per-route quotas. We can set per-key QPS caps and integrate an adaptive throttling layer so you don't blow your SLA. We also support token-based quotas and can export those metrics.
11:36 Lina Ortiz: does Redwood surface headers for remaining quota so the app can back off?
11:41 Priya Singh: yes we return X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and a Retry-After for when throttled; for Dedicated you can turn on per-route tracing to emit logs to your S3 or ELK.

14:50 Omar Haddad: observability — our SREs want traces and per-request metadata (model id, model version, latency breakdown, tokens in/out). How does Redwood expose that?
15:01 Priya Singh: console offers per-route dashboard with token-level breakdowns, but for programmatic hooks we have: structured logs with per-request JSON (model, latency, tokens, route), an event export to your Kinesis/CloudPubSub, and tracing headers (W3C traceparent) so you can stitch Redwood calls into your distributed traces. We also provide a webhook for anomaly alerts.
15:37 Daniel Park: any observability cost? like do you charge for log export retention?
15:42 Alex Chen: audit logs and high retention are an add-on. Basic observability is included but high retention or streaming exports are add-on features on enterprise plans.

18:20 Lina Ortiz: security questions — SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS, and SSO (SAML). Also for private deployments we need help with HSM/KMS integration.
18:31 Priya Singh: we are SOC2 Type II, support SAML/Okta, and for Hosted we encrypt CSM data at rest with customer-provided KMS (bring-your-own-key) on enterprise tier. Dedicated/Private supports HSM integration and customer-managed KMS. I'll attach the security pack with the specifics and the contact for our security team.

21:10 Daniel Park: model variants and fallbacks — we want to degrade gracefully when capacity is constrained. How do rollouts and fallbacks work?
21:22 Priya Singh: you can configure routing policies: prefer low-latency model but fall back to cheaper quantized variants or different region. We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. For Dedicated you can pin a model version to a pool to avoid surprises.

24:45 Lina Ortiz: on evaluation — we'd like to run a POC: hosted first for speed, then Dedicated if latency/cost justify. We will need an integration checklist and example workloads.
24:56 Alex Chen: totally reasonable. Our typical flow: 1) small hosted pilot (1k-5k req/day) with LangChain examples, 2) measure latency/cost and run our batching/caching suggestions, 3) if needed, spin up a Dedicated evaluation with reserved pool for a week of benchmarking.
25:18 Priya Singh: for the hosted POC we'll provide a sample dataset, embedding scripts, and a script to capture trace headers so you can ingest into your observability stack.

27:05 Omar Haddad: what about IP allowlisting for hosted — can we lock to our egress?
27:12 Alex Chen: yes you can provide static egress IPs to allowlist, and we also support short-lived mTLS certs if you need mutual auth.

30:00 Daniel Park: cost modeling — can you share a sample cost calculation for embeddings + rerank + generation?
30:10 Alex Chen: yes i'll send a sample calc comparing hosted per-token pricing vs dedicated hourly + GPU amortized; we'll include quantized runs to show delta. For semantic search embeddings are often the main driver; we recommend batching and caching embeddings and incremental indexing.

33:20 Lina Ortiz: integration with LlamaIndex — does Redwood provide direct embedding backend hooks so LlamaIndex can call embeddings without proxying through our service?
33:33 Priya Singh: you can call our embeddings API directly from your indexer. We have a native LlamaIndex connector that plugs into the embeddings generator. If you want to isolate traffic we can recommend running an internal proxy that handles keys and rotate tokens.

36:15 Omar Haddad: for the gateway/proxy setup — do you have a sample helm chart or k8s manifests?
36:23 Priya Singh: yes we have a sample gateway helm chart for Dedicated/Private that sets up ingress, mTLS, and a sidecar for metrics. We'll share that repo.

38:40 Daniel Park: outstanding concerns: data residency for EU customers and PII — we'll need contractual language and details on delete-on-demand workflows.
38:50 Alex Chen: noted, we'll include deletion SLA and an EU-region hosting map in the security pack and legal addendum.

41:05 Alex Chen: recap — action items and next steps?
41:12 Daniel Park: i'll get you the prompt sets and sample documents by Friday 2026-04-09.
41:18 Lina Ortiz: i'll join the POC kickoff and provide target QPS.
41:22 Omar Haddad: i'll review the helm chart and send network requirements.
41:30 Alex Chen: we'll send the integration guide, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, security pack, and pricing bands; schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-04-12.

42:05 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and next steps.

Notes on transcript quality: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (on-premision -> on-prem, mTLS as em-TLS sometimes), speaker labels occasionally overlap.
